Every nondegenerate centrally symmetric convex hexagon is t+[-a,a]+[-b,b]+[-c,c]; its exact zonotope area is 4(X+Y+Z). For fixed independent outward covectors u,v, the tight enclosing parallelogram area is 4h_P(u)h_P(v)/|det(u,v)|. On the normal fan each h_P(u) is linear; for fixed v and fixed determinant sign this quotient is linear fractional and bounded below by an extremal edge-normal ray; denominator-zero boundaries diverge because P has interior. Replace u, then v of a global optimum by such rays without worsening the optimum, reducing unrestricted minimization to exactly three distinct hexagon side-pair directions. Coordinates c=αa+βb give tight Q_ab=4(X+Y)(X+Z)/X=4(T+XYZ/X²); minimizing cyclic choices picks M=max(X,Y,Z), so q=4(T+XYZ/M²). Normalizing max 1, middle s, min r gives ratio 1+rs/(1+r+s), monotone in s; sharp deficit ≥2(1-r)/(3(2+r)) realized by a=(1,0), b=(0,1), c=(-1,r), and inverse bound r≥(2-6eps)/(2+3eps). Checked bundled exact sympy/rational hull assertions and independently reconstructed the analytic minimization: sampled candidate polygons would NOT suffice for all orientation proof.
